title: Elementary magnons and interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles in the effective spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ kagome-staircase magnet Co$_{3}$V$_{2}$O$_{8}$
authors: Yuan Xiao, Jiajun Mo, Zhenmeng Jiang, Haoyang Leng, Otkur Omar, Yanjun Li, Fengyi Song, Jianjun Ying, Shang Gao
abstract: The excitation spectrum of an anisotropic magnet provides a direct link between its microscopic Hamiltonian and interaction-driven quasiparticles. Here we use high-resolution time-domain terahertz spectroscopy to map the magnetic excitations of the three-dimensional kagome-staircase compound Co$_{3}$V$_{2}$O$_{8}$ as functions of temperature and magnetic field. At low energies, polarization-resolved spectra identify magnetic-dipole-active one-magnon modes and track their evolution across the ferromagnetic and spin-density-wave phases. Combining their field dependence with previously reported inelastic-neutron-scattering dispersions, we determine an effective spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ Hamiltonian with strongly anisotropic exchange that quantitatively reproduces the one-magnon spectrum. This model provides a noninteracting benchmark for the high-energy response, where we observe sharp branches with field slopes that are two to four times those of the one-magnon modes, together with anticrossings between branches of different magnon numbers. Their sharpness, polarization dependence, and departure from the calculated multi-magnon continua identify them as interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles that can be stabilized by strong exchange anisotropy.
summary: This paper investigates the magnetic excitations in Co3V2O8 using terahertz spectroscopy. By fitting low-energy one-magnon modes to an effective spin-1/2 Hamiltonian derived from combined experimental data, the authors successfully identify higher-energy features as interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles. This work demonstrates how strong exchange anisotropy stabilizes these complex excitations beyond simple non-interacting models.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the magnetic excitation spectrum of the kagome-staircase magnet Co3V2O8, specifically distinguishing between elementary one-magnon modes and interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles.
main_result: High-energy excitations observed via terahertz spectroscopy are identified as sharp, interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles stabilized by strong exchange anisotropy, which cannot be explained by non-interacting models.
method: The research combines high-resolution time-domain terahertz spectroscopy (TDTS) measurements with theoretical modeling based on an effective spin-1/2 anisotropic-exchange Hamiltonian derived from fitting both TDTS and inelastic neutron scattering data.
model_or_system: The physical system is the three-dimensional kagome-staircase compound Co3V2O8. The analysis utilizes an effective spin-1/2 model with strong anisotropic exchange interactions to describe the magnetic excitations.
key_observables: Polarization-resolved low-energy one-magnon modes, and high-energy sharp branches exhibiting field slopes two to four times those of single magnons, along with evidence of avoided crossings (hybridization).
important_parameters: Temperature (T), external magnetic field (B), exchange coupling constants (J1, J3, J4, J6), and the effective spin-1/2 Hamiltonian parameters.
main_assumptions: The low-energy dynamics can be effectively described by a spin-1/2 model; the analysis combines zone-center TDTS data with momentum-dependent INS data for comprehensive fitting.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure, experimental setups (TDTS), phase diagrams showing magnetic transitions (FM, SDW), and frequency spectra revealing both single-magnon and multi-magnon responses across varying fields and temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the material's magnetic phases and uses TDTS to map low-energy one-magnon modes. It then fits these data alongside INS results to determine an effective Hamiltonian. Finally, it analyzes high-energy features, identifying them as interacting multi-magnon quasiparticles through evidence of hybridization.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed experimental and theoretical framework for understanding collective excitations in frustrated magnets, which is highly relevant to modeling strongly correlated quantum materials where magnon interactions are key.
